producer_report.summary: I revised the design note, the roadmap and the changelog to fix the three findings; only docs changed. Section 7 of the note no longer claims a push refusal. It cites Git::push_branch (lib.rs lines 430-436): a plain push to a new branch is never refused because main moved. Detection moves to just before the host merge (MergeMethod in gh/client.rs). The job refetches and checks with is_ancestor that the PR's parent is still the main tip, with an optional host up-to-date requirement as a second guard. If main moved, it rebuilds with merge_tree and pushes under a fresh branch name. Each case has a concrete signal. Sections 3 and 6 now score the 5.0-minute prediction against the verifier-to-first-record stage (about 4.6 minutes) and say the headline 2984.3 median is not the figure compared with 5.0. The roadmap item is renumbered from 3b to 4, and the old item 4 becomes 5. The changelog entry is updated. `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` passes (22 tests). I did not run the full cargo build, fmt, clippy or full test suite.

criteria_check.criterion: Fixes finding 1 (major) of job 20261111-055238-5har: the section on host main moving and two jobs landing at once does not claim a push refusal. It states, citing Git::push_branch in crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs (about lines 430-436) that a plain push to a new PR branch is refused only when the branch exists and is not a descendant, so a main move does not fail the push. It names the real detection point: the host merge (gh/client.rs MergeMethod) preceded by an is_ancestor check that the PR's parent is still the main tip (or a host up-to-date requirement), then refetch and rebuild with merge_tree, with a concrete failure signal per case.
criteria_check.evidence: Section 7 rewritten. It cites push_branch lines 430-436, which I read in lib.rs, and says a main move never fails the push. It puts detection before the host merge (MergeMethod in gh/client.rs line 416) with an is_ancestor check and an optional host up-to-date setting, and gives a signal per case (parent equals tip, main moved, host refuses the merge anyway, two jobs at once). The rebuild uses merge_tree and a fresh branch name.

open_issues: The roadmap still has item 3a (CI routing) next to the plain numbers. It was already there, so I left it; renumber it if you want a purely numeric list.
The host up-to-date requirement is a repository setting I could not check from here. The note labels it an option, not a measured behavior.
mistakes: My first draft of the moved-main bullet was muddled about pushing to the same branch name. I rewrote it to push under a fresh branch name.
learnings: Git::push_branch is a plain push at lib.rs lines 430-436, so a moved main never fails a push to a new branch. The race is at the host merge, a MergeMethod in gh/client.rs.
